thread:
morgan: Quick flag from the reranker bring-up: candidate-xp1 (hybrid-4bit) shows NDCG@10 +0.5% but MRR -3.1% on longtail-eval-v2.

sarah: That's concerning. Usually MRR and ndcg move together. Can you paste the eval command and a sample diff?

morgan: Sure:
```
python tools/eval_rerank.py --model candidate-xp1 --dataset longtail-eval-v2 --format "query
||doc" --metrics ndcg@10,mrr,ndcg@1 --seed 42
```
results: ndcg@10: 0.648 (+0.005), mrr: 0.284 (-0.031), ndcg@1: 0.512 (-0.022)
```

lee: ndcg@1 drop explains MRR drop (top1 worse). What changed in candidate-xp1 vs baseline?

morgan: Two diffs: switched to hf fast tokenizer and changed delimiter to include newline between query and doc. Also applied hybrid 4-bit quant to attention.

anil: Tokenizer + delimiter can change token boundaries; quant can amplify. We should isolate each variable.

morgan: I'm running three variants: (A) xp1 + fast tokenizer (current), (B) xp1 + slow tokenizer, (C) baseline weights (no quant) + fast tokenizer.

ops-bot: Job queued 2112234450 eval-A (xp1 + fast)
ops-bot: Job queued 2112234466 eval-B (xp1 + slow)
ops-bot: Job queued 2112234500 eval-C (baseline + fast)

sarah: Also slice results by doc-type. longtail-eval-v2 contains HTML-heavy docs where punctuation tokenization changes are more common.

morgan: Added slices: html-heavy, short-query, long-query. Also computing ndcg@1 to focus on top1 flips.

morgan: Interim results:
- eval-A (xp1 + fast): ndcg@10 0.648, mrr 0.284, ndcg@1 0.512
- eval-B (xp1 + slow): ndcg@10 0.641, mrr 0.299, ndcg@1 0.536
- eval-C (baseline + fast): ndcg@10 0.639, mrr 0.297, ndcg@1 0.534

anil: Looks like quant + fast tokenizer combo is the culprit. With slow tokenizer MRR improves despite quant.

lee: Action items: 1) enforce tokenizer parity in onboarding checklist (pick fast or slow and normalize golden sets), 2) add token-boundary regression test to eval harness (compare ndcg@1 on tokenized-length-change slice), 3) run small per-layer attention scale sweep for quant calibration.

sarah: And add a slice for short queries with heavy punctuation; most top1 flips live there.

morgan: I'll update the onboarding checklist and open a ticket for per-layer quant scaling. For immediate canary, I'll revert to the old delimiter (no newline) so we don't conflate effects.

lee: I can help with the calibration job. Ping me when jobs are up.

morgan: Thanks — kicking off the calibration sweep and will post results. TL;DR: MRR drop reproducible when hybrid-4bit quant + fast tokenizer + newline delimiter are combined; next steps: standardize tokenizer, add tests, run quant calibration, revert delimiter for canary. :thumbsup:
